chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife three times in one sitting. He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) returned to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar his wife, as he had divorced her three times while she was menstruating. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) annulled that divorce and said: "Everything that contradicts the Book of Allah and the Sunnah is returned to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah."'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on triple divorce in one sitting according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the Shia jurisprudential stance that a triple divorce pronounced in one sitting is treated as a single revocable divorce (raj'i), based on the Prophet's correction of Ibn 'Umar's practice. It establishes the principle of 'returning to the Book and Sunnah' for any ruling that contradicts them, emphasizing the authority of the Prophet's practical interpretation over mere textual occurrence. This view contrasts with the Sunni majority opinion which often considers it a final divorce (ba'in), underscoring the Shia reliance on the Prophet's specific actions as legislative precedent.
